scenes.text: Koalas have fingerprints almost identical to yours.
In the nineteen nineties, a scientist in Australia looked at them under a microscope.
He found koala prints were practically impossible to tell apart from human ones.
Koalas are the only animals outside the primates known to have them.
Our last shared ancestor lived over a hundred million years ago, so we evolved them separately.
Scientists think the ridges help koalas grip branches and eucalyptus leaves.
Could a koala fool a detective?

title: Koalas have fingerprints like humans 🐨
caption: Under a microscope, koala fingerprints are nearly indistinguishable from ours. They evolved them separately from primates, probably to grip branches and leaves. 🐨
